polityNote: Republic of South Africa from the nine-province constitution of 1994-04-27 (Interim Constitution). Atoms are the 213 local and metropolitan municipalities of geoBoundaries ZAF ADM3 (Municipal Demarcation Board, 2016 demarcation, release year 2020); a province is the union of the municipalities that lie in it (each of the 213 lies 100% in one province of the gb ADM1 release from the same source). Province lines have been municipal lines since the Twelfth Amendment (2006-03-01) and can change only by constitutional amendment (Sixteenth Amendment 2009-04-03, Merafong City; none since), so the 2016 municipalities carry the 2009+ provinces exactly. Before 1994-04-27 the four provinces 1910–1994 are answered by OpenHistoricalMap (relations 2691750/2691753/2691754/2691755) and are not reconstructed here. Independent check (①): union area / Stats SA Census 2011 province area — WC 129,527/129,462 = 1.0005, EC 169,082/168,966 = 1.0007, NC 373,352/372,889 = 1.0012, FS 130,008/129,825 = 1.0014, KZN 94,492/94,361 = 1.0014, NW 105,077/104,882 = 1.0019, GP 18,213/18,178 = 1.0019, MP 76,642/76,495 = 1.0019, LP 126,044/125,754 = 1.0023 (all within 0.25%, spherical area of the atoms).

unresolved.what: Seven provinces before the Twelfth Amendment (1994 boundaries)
unresolved.why: Between 1994 and 2006 the provincial lines followed the 1994 magisterial districts, and from 2000-12-05 the cross-boundary municipalities (Bushbuckridge, Greater Groblersdal, Greater Marble Hall, Greater Tubatse, Kungwini, Nokeng tsa Taemane, City of Tshwane, Merafong City, Moshaweng, Kagisano, Ga-Segonyana, Phokwane area, Matatiele, Umzimkulu …) straddled them. The 12th Amendment assigned each to one province, so the 1994 lines run INSIDE today's municipalities: no union of the 213 ADM3 atoms (the finest gbOpen level for ZAF) draws them.
